jewelry-watch-accessories.summary: A few well-chosen rings, chains or a watch finish an outfit and add instant polish and a hint of taste or status.

quick.overview:
Jewelry, watches and other accessories are used to make an outfit look finished. A simple watch, a ring or a thin chain adds polish the moment it goes on, and signals taste or status with little effort.

The chain is direct: add a few pieces, the outfit reads as complete, and the overall look comes across as tasteful. Jewellery has a long history as a marker of status and group identity, and the wristwatch went from a military tool to a fashion and status item. No trials have tested accessories against attractiveness ratings.
quick.how: Style communities favour minimal choices: one watch, one or two rings, perhaps a simple chain, matched to the outfit and the setting. Pieces range from inexpensive to luxury, and the effect shows immediately, with no waiting period.
quick.risks: Risk is low. Cultural norms about what counts as tasteful vary by place and setting, and counterfeit luxury watches are common, so buyers who want a genuine luxury piece need to check the seller.

angle.text: Minimal jewelry and a good watch finish an outfit and signal taste or status with little effort. The added polish is visible the moment the pieces go on. Accessories have not been tested in attractiveness trials.

grooming-routine-nails-ear-nose-hair.summary: Trimmed nails and tidy ear and nose hair clean up the details people notice up close, for a more put-together look.

quick.overview:
A grooming routine covering nails and ear and nose hair is basic upkeep that makes you look neater and more polished up close. Clean, trimmed nails and tidy hair in the ears and nose remove small details that can otherwise read as unkempt.

The change is visible right after grooming. Trimming nails is listed among standard hygiene practices, and grooming is distinguished from hygiene as the part that supports a good appearance. No study has tested these habits against attractiveness ratings.
quick.how: People fold it into a regular routine: trimming and cleaning fingernails and toenails, and trimming ear and nose hair with a small trimmer or scissors. It is usually done alongside shaving, haircuts and skin care, and the results are immediate.
quick.risks: Risk is low. Sources describe no specific harms; as with any trimming tool, small nicks are possible, so careful use around the nose and ears is sensible.

angle.text: Tidy nails and trimmed ear and nose hair raise perceived polish, and the change shows right after grooming. Appearance communities treat it as basic upkeep that makes the whole look cleaner and more put-together.

skin-care-baseline-routine.summary: Cleanser, moisturiser and daily SPF: the base routine for clearer, more even skin and slower visible sun aging.

quick.overview:
The baseline routine is a gentle cleanser, a moisturiser and a daily broad-spectrum sunscreen. People use it to get clearer, smoother, more even skin and to slow visible aging, and communities treat it as the foundation before adding any active ingredients or procedures.

The chain: cleansing removes oil and residue, moisturiser slows water loss from the skin, and sunscreen filters UV light that drives sunburn, photoaging and skin cancer. Sunscreen has the most research behind it, with studies reporting reduced sunburn and skin cancer risk and slower photoaging. Dermatology sources describe the same trio as the generally favoured approach, with other products reserved for conditions like acne.
quick.how: Cleanse in the morning and evening, moisturise after, and apply sunscreen each morning, reapplying when outdoors for long. Most people start here and add other products only once the basics are steady. Skin changes from sun protection build over months and years.
quick.risks: Risks are low. Fragrances or preservatives can cause contact dermatitis, harsh cleansers or over-exfoliation can irritate, and sunscreen protection depends on how much is applied. Paraffin-based moisturisers carry a documented fire risk near flames.

angle.text: Cleanser, moisturiser and daily sunscreen are the base layer people build skin quality on, aiming for clearer, more even skin and slower visible aging. Sunscreen works by blocking the UV that drives photoaging, and studies back that part most strongly.

style-subreddit-fit-check-culture-r-male.summary: Post an outfit photo to communities like r/malefashionadvice and get free critique on fit, colour and layering from other members.

quick.overview:
Fit-check culture means posting a photo of your outfit online and getting feedback. The best known venue is r/malefashionadvice, a Reddit community founded in 2009 with millions of members, where men share outfits, ask shopping questions and get help identifying garments.

The chain: you post a photo, members point out fit and colour issues, and you adjust what you buy and wear. It works as crowd feedback in place of a personal stylist, and the payoff shows in better-fitting, better-chosen outfits. No studies have measured whether the feedback changes how attractive people are rated.
quick.how: Users post photos in recurring outfit threads or ask targeted questions, then read the comments and apply the advice to later purchases and outfits. Many come back with updated fits over weeks or months to track progress.
quick.risks: Risks are minimal. Posting photos has privacy implications, and advice quality varies with who responds. The community's moderation was disrupted during the 2023 Reddit API protest.

angle.text: Users post outfit photos to communities like r/malefashionadvice and collect critique on fit, colour and layering. They then change what they buy and wear, so better-fitting, better-chosen clothes are what change their look.

style-ai-apps-virtual-try-on.summary: Apps that preview clothes, accessories or looks on your own photo or camera view, so you can test styles before buying.

quick.overview:
Style AI apps and virtual try-on tools overlay clothes or looks on a photo or live camera view of you, and some suggest outfits automatically. People use them to see a style on themselves before they buy or commit.

The chain: preview on your own image, narrow down what suits you, then buy clothes that look better on you. The tools combine camera input, body or face measurements and 3D or image-based rendering, with augmented reality tracking movement in live video. No independent evaluation of how closely previews match real results was found.
quick.how: People upload a photo or use the camera, try several garments, colours or accessories, and shortlist the ones they like before shopping. Many use them as a browsing aid alongside size guides and reviews.
quick.risks: Documented limits include fixed-distance requirements, self-measurement errors and sensitivity to lighting. Uploading face or body images raises privacy concerns, and accuracy has not been independently tested.

angle.text: Virtual try-on and style apps let you preview clothing, accessories or hairstyles on your own photo before you commit. The preview narrows your choices, and the outfit or look you pick is what changes your appearance.

hairstyle-simulators-ai-haircut-preview.summary: Preview a haircut on your own selfie to pick a style that suits your face before you visit a stylist.

quick.overview:
Hairstyle simulators place a chosen cut or colour on a photo of your face, and AI versions generate the style rather than overlaying a template. People use them to find a cut that suits their face shape before sitting in a barber's chair.

The chain: upload a selfie, see several styles on your own face, and take the best match to your stylist. The app detects the face and head, then renders the hairstyle. Reference sources say face shape, hair type and head shape affect real-world results. No studies have tested how closely previews match the finished cut.
quick.how: Users upload a front-facing photo, cycle through cuts and colours, save favourites and show screenshots to their barber or stylist, who adjusts them for the person's actual hair.
quick.risks: Risks are low. Previews may not reflect hair texture, density or growth patterns, and uploading face photos raises privacy concerns.

angle.text: Users upload a selfie to see a haircut on their own face before visiting a stylist, aiming to choose a cut that suits their face shape. The haircut itself is what changes appearance, and the preview helps pick the right one.

testosterone-gel-androgel.summary: Prescription skin-applied testosterone for diagnosed low T, studied for gains in lean mass and drops in fat mass in hypogonadal men.

quick.overview:
Testosterone gel is a prescription gel applied to the skin to treat low testosterone in men; AndroGel is the best-known brand. Its appearance interest comes from muscle and body composition: leaner, more muscular physiques once levels are restored.

The chain: testosterone is absorbed through the skin, circulating levels rise, and lean mass tends to go up while fat mass goes down. Studies in hypogonadal men report normalised testosterone and improvements in sexual function, mood, lean mass and bone density. Cosmetic use in men with normal levels is off-label and less studied.
quick.how: It is used as a daily gel under a prescriber's direction, often by men who want a steady alternative to injections. Lab monitoring is part of routine care, and body-composition changes in trials build over months.
quick.risks: Reported effects include acne, breast enlargement, raised hematocrit and sperm suppression, with cardiovascular and clot concerns discussed for testosterone products. Skin contact can transfer it to women and children, and virilisation has occurred in exposed people. It is a controlled substance needing a prescription in most countries.

angle.text: Testosterone gel is prescribed for diagnosed low testosterone, and users discuss it as a TRT option for muscle, body composition and energy. Trials in hypogonadal men show gains in lean mass and drops in fat mass; use for looks in men with normal levels is off-label.

nasal-testosterone-natesto.summary: Prescription testosterone nasal gel for diagnosed low T, noted in TRT circles for possibly keeping sperm production and gonadotropins intact.

quick.overview:
Natesto is a prescription testosterone gel given through the nose for men with low testosterone. People on TRT discuss it because small studies suggest it may keep sperm production and gonadotropins more intact than other testosterone forms.

The appearance link is the usual TRT one: restored testosterone supports muscle and lower fat. Trials in hypogonadal men report normalised testosterone, and several small studies report preserved semen parameters. A 90-day trial of 306 hypogonadal men found the nasal gel normalised androgen levels, with extensions to one year. These studies are in medical patients, not cosmetic users.
quick.how: It is short-acting, so it is applied several times a day under a prescriber's direction. It suits people who want an alternative to skin gels or injections and who care about fertility.
quick.risks: As with other testosterone products, reported concerns include raised hematocrit, blood pressure monitoring, acne, and prostate and cardiovascular questions. It is a controlled prescription drug and is banned in competitive sport.

angle.text: Natesto is a prescription nasal testosterone for diagnosed low T, popular in TRT circles because small studies suggest it may keep sperm production more intact. The looks link is the usual TRT one, more muscle and less fat, studied in hypogonadal men.

oral-testosterone-undecanoate-jatenzo-ky.summary: Prescription testosterone capsules taken by mouth for diagnosed deficiency, a needle-free TRT option aimed at supporting lean mass and less fat.

quick.overview:
Oral testosterone undecanoate is a prescription capsule form of testosterone replacement. Jatenzo was approved by the US FDA in 2019 as the first oral version, followed by Tlando and Kyzatrex in 2022, for adult men with low or absent testosterone from specific medical causes.

In muscle-focused communities it is discussed as a needle-free alternative to injections or gels. The appearance link is the usual TRT one: restored testosterone supports lean mass and lower fat. Published trials are in men with deficiency; none examine physique or facial appearance in healthy men.
quick.how: Capsules are taken by mouth with food under a prescriber's direction, since absorption is reported to rise with fatty food and to vary between individuals. Blood pressure and hormone levels are monitored during use.
quick.risks: Reported effects include raised blood pressure, acne, hair growth, raised liver enzymes and lipid changes, and US labels carry blood pressure warnings. Testosterone products in general can suppress sperm production. It is a Schedule III controlled substance in the US and requires a prescription.

angle.text: Oral testosterone undecanoate is a prescription capsule form of TRT for diagnosed deficiency, discussed as an alternative to injections or gels. The looks link is the usual TRT one, more lean mass and less fat, studied in men with low testosterone.

testosterone-pellets-testopel.summary: Rice-grain testosterone implants placed under the skin that release hormone for months, an established TRT option for muscle and body composition.

quick.overview:
Testosterone pellets are small solid implants placed under the skin that release testosterone gradually. Testopel is the FDA-approved brand; the US approved implantable pellets in 1972 for testosterone deficiency. People choose them to avoid frequent injections or daily gels while keeping the muscle and body-composition benefits of restored testosterone.

The chain: pellets dissolve slowly, steady testosterone enters the bloodstream, and lean mass and fat mass shift in the usual TRT direction. Published work consists mainly of observational serum-level studies, patient-preference surveys and a few small randomised trials in men with diagnosed deficiency. None examine appearance in healthy people.
quick.how: A clinician inserts the pellets under the skin in a minor office procedure, typically in the hip or buttock area, and they release hormone over several months before the next set is placed. It appeals to people who want infrequent dosing.
quick.risks: The procedure can cause infection or pellet extrusion. As with other testosterone therapy, effects include acne, raised red blood cell counts, sperm suppression and other systemic effects. Compounded pellets are not the same as the branded FDA-approved product.

angle.text: Testosterone pellets are implants under the skin that release hormone for months, used by people on TRT who prefer fewer doses. The looks link is more muscle and less fat from restored testosterone, supported by observational data and small trials in men with deficiency.

testosterone-undecanoate-injection-aveed.summary: Long-acting testosterone injection given in a clinic every few months for diagnosed deficiency, with a REMS programme for lung oil-embolism and anaphylaxis risk.

quick.overview:
Testosterone undecanoate injection is a long-acting testosterone depot sold as Aveed in the US and Nebido in Europe. It is given in a medical setting to men with testosterone deficiency, and people on TRT discuss it as a way to avoid frequent self-injection while keeping the usual muscle and lean-mass benefits.

The chain: the ester dissolves in oil and releases slowly from the muscle depot, where it is converted to testosterone; reported intramuscular half-life is around 21 days in tea seed oil and 34 days in castor oil. Registered studies cover long-term safety, blood pressure and other outcomes in hypogonadal men. None examine cosmetic outcomes.
quick.how: It is administered by a clinician at intervals of weeks to months, so visits replace daily or weekly routines. Aveed requires observation after injection under its safety programme.
quick.risks: The FDA rejected Aveed in 2008, 2009 and 2013 over pulmonary oil microembolism (POME) and anaphylaxis concerns before approving it in 2014 with a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy. Other reported effects are acne, hypertension, raised liver enzymes and lipid changes. It is a Schedule III controlled substance in the US.

angle.text: Aveed is a long-acting, clinic-administered testosterone injection for diagnosed deficiency, appealing to people who want infrequent dosing. The looks link is the usual TRT one, more lean mass and less fat, studied in men with low testosterone.

sustanon-testosterone-blend.summary: A blend of four testosterone esters in oil, discussed in bodybuilding circles for building muscle and size.

quick.overview:
Sustanon is the brand name for mixed-ester testosterone injections. Sustanon 250 combines four esters (propionate, phenylpropionate, isocaproate and decanoate), and Sustanon 100 combines three. It is discussed in bodybuilding circles for building muscle and a fuller physique.

The chain: after intramuscular injection each ester is cleaved to release testosterone, with shorter esters acting sooner and longer ones lasting longer, so the blend spreads release over time. Testosterone's effects on lean mass are well documented in general. This specific blend has little published research of its own and no appearance trials.
quick.how: It is an injectable used in TRT and in bodybuilding circles, valued for mixing faster and slower release in one product. Muscle changes from testosterone build over weeks to months.
quick.risks: General testosterone risks include acne, sperm suppression, raised red blood cell counts and cardiovascular and prostate considerations. Testosterone is a controlled substance in many countries.

angle.text: Sustanon is a blended testosterone ester injection used in bodybuilding circles to build muscle and size by raising testosterone and protein synthesis. Testosterone's effect on lean mass is well documented; this blend has no appearance trials of its own.

cabergoline.summary: A prescription dopamine agonist that lowers prolactin, used for prolactinomas and discussed online as an add-on to hormone regimens.

quick.overview:
Cabergoline is an ergot-derived dopamine D2 agonist taken by mouth. Its labelled use is for high prolactin, including from pituitary adenomas. In muscle and TRT communities it is discussed as a way to manage prolactin during hormone therapy, so the regimen runs smoothly and supports muscle and libido goals.

The chain: it stimulates D2 receptors on prolactin-producing pituitary cells, mimicking dopamine and lowering prolactin; in prolactinomas it also shrinks tumours. Its half-life is long, reported around 63 to 115 hours. Published trials are in prolactinomas and other pituitary conditions, not in healthy people seeking appearance changes.
quick.how: It is taken by mouth under a prescriber's direction, usually alongside blood work that tracks prolactin. People using it in hormone regimens treat it as a supporting drug rather than a main one.
quick.risks: Common effects are nausea, headache, dizziness and constipation. Ergot-derived dopamine agonists have been linked to cardiac valve regurgitation, mainly at high Parkinson's-disease doses, and the label advises cardiovascular evaluation including echocardiography. Rare pulmonary and other fibrotic complications are reported. It is prescription-only.

angle.text: Cabergoline lowers prolactin and is discussed as an add-on to testosterone or other hormone regimens to manage prolactin side effects. The looks link is indirect: a smoother regimen is meant to support muscle and libido goals. Trials have studied it in prolactinomas.

fsh-menopur-hmg.summary: Fertility gonadotropins (FSH, hMG) from IVF medicine, used in TRT circles to keep sperm production and testicular function going alongside testosterone.

quick.overview:
Menopur is a brand of purified menotropin (human menopausal gonadotropin, hMG), a mixture of FSH and LH activity originally extracted from the urine of postmenopausal women. It is used to stimulate the ovaries in fertility treatment, and the same drug class can stimulate sperm production in hypogonadal men.

In TRT communities these gonadotropins come up as fertility-preserving companions to testosterone, keeping the testes active so natural hormone function is preserved while the regimen's muscle and body-composition goals continue. FSH acts on Sertoli cells in men to support sperm production, and LH activity stimulates sex-hormone production. The published trials are almost all in women having IVF; none examine appearance.
quick.how: These are prescription injectables given under medical monitoring, mainly by people on testosterone therapy who want to maintain fertility. Recombinant FSH products supply FSH alone, while Menopur supplies both activities.
quick.risks: Known concerns in women's fertility treatment include ovarian overstimulation and multiple pregnancy. They are prescription drugs given by injection under monitoring. Specific harms in men using them alongside testosterone are not covered by the trials available.

angle.text: FSH and Menopur come from IVF medicine and are used in TRT circles to keep sperm production and testicular function going alongside testosterone. The looks link is sustaining a TRT regimen's muscle and body-composition goals; the trials are in fertility treatment.

fenugreek.summary: A culinary seed sold as an herbal testosterone and libido supplement, taken by lifters for better training and body composition.

quick.overview:
Fenugreek is a Mediterranean and South Asian plant whose seeds are used as a spice and in traditional medicine. In fitness circles it is sold as a natural testosterone booster, usually as seed extract capsules, taken by lifters hoping for better training results, libido and a leaner, more muscular physique.

The chain: seed compounds such as steroidal saponins are proposed to nudge testosterone, which supports training and body composition. A few small randomised trials of specific extracts, and meta-analyses of them, report higher total testosterone or sexual-function scores in some men. Reviewers note few studies, varied extracts and small samples, and human mechanistic data are limited.
quick.how: It is taken as seed extract capsules or powder, often inside multi-herb men's-health products and paired with training. Users report effects, if any, over weeks.
quick.risks: Reported side effects include diarrhea, bloating and gas, and a maple-like body odor. It may lower blood sugar and interfere with anticoagulants and diabetes drugs, and it is not considered safe in pregnancy. It is sold as a dietary supplement in the US, not an approved drug.

angle.text: Fenugreek seed extract is sold as a natural testosterone and libido supplement, taken by lifters hoping for better training results and body composition. Small trials of branded extracts report modest hormone changes in some men.

d-aspartic-acid-daa.summary: An amino acid sold as a testosterone booster for lifters; trials in trained men found no increase and, at higher intake, a decrease.

quick.overview:
D-aspartic acid is the D-form of the common amino acid aspartic acid, found naturally in the pituitary gland and testes. It is sold as a sports supplement marketed for raising testosterone, aimed at men who lift and want more muscle and a leaner physique.

The chain: laboratory work in rats proposes that D-aspartate acts in the pituitary to increase LH release and in the testes to raise testosterone synthesis. A 2009 study reported higher LH and testosterone in humans and rats. Randomised trials in resistance-trained men published between 2013 and 2017 found no testosterone rise, and one found lower testosterone at the higher intake tested.
quick.how: It is taken as a powder or capsule, typically for a few weeks alongside resistance training, and sometimes included in multi-ingredient testosterone-support products.
quick.risks: The trials report no major safety signals, but one found lower total and free testosterone at the higher intake, and another reported a 16 percent drop in estradiol. It is sold as a dietary supplement, and long-term safety data are limited.

angle.text: D-aspartic acid is sold as a testosterone booster for men who lift, aiming at better training response and more muscle. Early work suggested a hormonal role, while trials in trained men found no testosterone increase.

horny-goat-weed-epimedium.summary: A Chinese herb sold as a libido and erection supplement; its flavonoid icariin inhibits PDE5 in the lab.

quick.overview:
Horny goat weed refers to plants of the genus Epimedium, used for centuries in traditional Chinese medicine as a kidney and yang tonic. It is sold for libido, erections and vigour, and appears in testosterone-support stacks as part of a male-vitality routine.

The chain: icariin, its main flavonoid, is a weak PDE5 inhibitor in vitro, the same enzyme targeted by sildenafil and tadalafil but at far lower potency, and animal studies report improved erectile function through nitric oxide/cGMP signaling. Human trial evidence is minimal, and a recent review says clinical efficacy still needs confirmation in randomised trials.
quick.how: It is taken as capsules or extracts standardised to icariin, usually as one ingredient in multi-herb vitality or testosterone-support products.
quick.risks: Human safety data are limited. It is sold as a dietary supplement, and a US testosterone-support product listing it advises consulting a physician if pregnant or breastfeeding. Interaction data with PDE5 inhibitor drugs are not established.

angle.text: Horny goat weed is a Chinese herb sold for libido, erections and vigour, and it appears in testosterone-support stacks. People link it to male vitality and hormones; its flavonoid icariin shows PDE5 activity in lab work.

maca-root.summary: An Andean root vegetable sold as a libido and energy supplement, with a few trials suggesting a possible benefit for sexual desire.

quick.overview:
Maca is a radish-like root grown at high altitude in the Peruvian Andes, eaten as food for centuries and now sold as powder, capsules and extracts for libido, energy and fertility. It is included in testosterone-support stacks as part of a male-vitality routine.

A 2010 systematic review found four randomised trials, with two reporting improved sexual desire or function, one reporting an effect in men with erectile dysfunction and one finding no effect in cyclists; its authors called the evidence limited. A 2026 review reports improved libido in men-only and mixed-sex studies. The mechanism is not established, and maca does not appear to contain hormones.
quick.how: It is eaten or taken as powder, capsules or extract, often added to smoothies or multi-herb vitality products, with users reporting any effect over several weeks.
quick.risks: Maca has a long record as food in the Andes. Extracts contain MTCA, a compound that may act as an MAO inhibitor, and France's food-safety agency has warned consumers about powdered root, a concern others dispute on the grounds that boiling deactivates it.

angle.text: Maca is an Andean root sold as a libido and energy supplement and included in testosterone-support stacks. The looks link is a general male-vitality belief; a small number of trials suggest a possible benefit for sexual desire.

panax-ginseng.summary: A classic East Asian adaptogen root sold for energy, libido and testosterone support, used in male-vitality stacks.

quick.overview:
Panax ginseng is a perennial root herb from the Russian Far East, northeast China and Korea, central to traditional East Asian medicine as a tonic. It is processed as white or red ginseng and sold as capsules, extracts and drinks for energy, stress and sexual function, and it appears in hormone-support stacks.

Its active constituents are thought to be ginsenosides, which have been studied for effects on inflammation, vascular tone and nitric oxide signaling. In men with mild to moderate erectile dysfunction, a Cochrane review of nine placebo-controlled trials (587 men) found small improvements in erectile function that were likely not clinically meaningful, mostly on low-certainty evidence.
quick.how: It is taken as capsules, extracts, teas or drinks, often within multi-herb men's-health products, and users generally report any effect after several weeks of regular use.
quick.risks: Common side effects include headache, raised blood pressure, diarrhea, insomnia and rash. It can interact with prescription drugs such as warfarin, and use in pregnancy and breastfeeding is potentially unsafe.

angle.text: Panax ginseng is a traditional East Asian root sold for energy, libido and testosterone, and used in hormone-support stacks. The looks link is a general vitality belief; a Cochrane review found small effects on erectile function.

mucuna-pruriens.summary: A tropical bean rich in natural L-DOPA, used in Ayurveda and sold as a dopamine, libido and testosterone supplement.

quick.overview:
Mucuna pruriens is a climbing legume whose seeds contain roughly 3 to 6 percent L-DOPA, the precursor to dopamine. Ayurvedic tradition uses the seeds as a nerve tonic and aphrodisiac, and the powder is sold for mood, motivation, libido and male fertility. Online communities discuss it as a way to raise dopamine and drive.

The chain: L-DOPA is converted to dopamine by the enzyme aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase, and dopamine and drive are then linked to libido and testosterone. Human evidence is mainly in Parkinson's disease: a small crossover study of 8 patients found seed powder gave faster onset and longer on-time than standard levodopa/carbidopa. Fertility and testosterone claims rest on animal studies.
quick.how: It is taken as seed powder or capsules, sometimes paired with other supplements that users say modify the dopamine pathway. Users report effects, if any, within days to weeks.
quick.risks: L-DOPA sensitivity can cause nausea, vomiting, cramping, arrhythmias and low blood pressure, and people on MAO inhibitors are advised to avoid the plant. A forum user reported vomiting after taking many capsules. Contact with raw pod hairs causes severe itching.

angle.text: Mucuna pruriens is a bean rich in natural L-DOPA, sold as a dopamine, libido and testosterone supplement and discussed online as a way to push dopamine higher. Human studies exist mainly for Parkinson's disease.
